cards.text: Paul, a servant of Christ Jesus called to be an apostle, is almost done with his letter to the believers in Rome (Romans 1:1, 7), and now he's saying goodbye. If you've ever tried to leave a party, you know goodbyes take a WHILE. First up, he commends Phoebe, a sister in the faith and a servant of the church in Cenchrea.

cards.question: Phoebe is a servant of the church in Cenchrea. What does Paul tell the believers in Rome to do for her?

answers.text: Welcome her and help with anything she needs
Send her straight on to Jerusalem
Find her a ship headed for Spain

cards.question: Paul says Phoebe has been a great help to him alone.

cards.text: Then Paul sends greetings to name after name after NAME: fellow workers, fellow prisoners, beloved friends, households and women who have worked hard in the Lord. Prisca and Aquila even risked their lives for him. And Rufus's mother has been a mother to Paul as well, and as a stamper who ended up Papa to six little cookie cutters, I RESPECT that. Then Paul tells them to greet one another with a holy kiss, and he says all the churches of Christ send greetings.

Then Paul's tone shifts, and he urges them to watch out for those who create divisions and obstacles contrary to the teaching they have learned. It's the same heads-up I give every new baker: "Welcome, friend, and watch out for the spilled sprinkles by the oven, because those things will take you DOWN."

cards.question: Paul tells the believers in Rome what to do about people who create divisions. What is it?

cards.text: Paul says these people are not serving our Lord Christ. And he says they have a way of fooling the naive.

cards.question: The people who cause divisions aren't serving our Lord Christ. What are they serving instead?
Paul warns that the people who cause divisions fool the naive with loud threats.

cards.text: Their trick is smooth talk and flattery. Friend, when somebody tells me my chef's hat looks EXTRA tall today, I already know they're after the last batch.
Then Paul turns to the believers in Rome themselves, and he says he rejoices over them.

cards.question: Paul rejoices over the believers in Rome. Why?

answers.text: Everyone has heard about their obedience
Their church has grown so quickly
They have sent him a generous gift

cards.question: Paul wants the believers in Rome to be wise about what is good and innocent about what is ___.

cards.text: Then Paul tells them something about the God of peace and Satan.

cards.question: Paul says that the God of peace will soon crush Satan under the believers' feet.

cards.text: Then Paul says, "The grace of our Lord Jesus Christ be with you." That sure sounds like a goodbye.
But wait, the people with Paul start sending greetings too, beginning with Timothy, his fellow worker.
Lucius, Jason and Sosipater, Paul's fellow countrymen, send greetings as well. Then a brand new voice speaks up in the letter to greet them in the Lord: Tertius.

cards.question: A new voice in Paul's letter greets the believers in Rome. Who is Tertius?

answers.text: The one who wrote down this letter
The one who will carry this letter
The leader of the church in Rome

cards.text: Tertius writes down this WHOLE letter and gets ONE line to say hi, like the coworker who types up the entire report and squeezes in one "hi" at the very bottom. Then even more greetings roll in.

cards.question: Gaius sends the believers in Rome greetings. What is Gaius known for?

cards.text: Erastus, the city treasurer, sends greetings, and so does our brother Quartus. Even the city treasurer wants in on this goodbye!
And Paul goes out BIG, with praise to Him who is able to strengthen them by Paul's gospel and the proclamation of Jesus Christ. Then Paul brings up a mystery concealed for ages past.

cards.question: Paul says the mystery concealed for ages past stays hidden.
Paul says the mystery is made known through the writings of the prophets, to lead all ___ to the obedience that comes from faith.
Paul ends the whole letter with glory forever to the only wise God. Through whom?
